purpose: Correct the prior suppression-planning node by incorporating the omitted 10-14 Feb Ramree feint, which provides a real RN Bay/Arakan-direction cue before SLEUTH.
retained_from_v001: 7-Feb hostile reconnaissance remains a bounded Japanese Ceylon surveillance probe and does not yield target-quality Trincomalee intelligence.
No retroactive Trincomalee bomber strike is created.
SLEUTH itself remains undetected at weapon-quality level and is not a Japanese trigger.
After HAILSTONE/CATCHPOLE, low-cost submarine/recon suppression dominates over discretionary major surface/air diversion.

effects: no maintained track, no strike, no surface intercept
Maintain Ceylon exit/Bay surveillance and submarine emphasis
Do not release second surface package; Central-Pacific opportunity cost remains high

preferred_operation_concept: Ceylon/Bay surveillance + submarine ambush + conditional land-based bomber strike only on fresh high-value track. Oyodo group remains a contact-exploitation reserve, not a blind raider.
planning_judgment: Japan is motivated enough to prepare to hurt the Eastern Fleet if it exposes itself, but not motivated/comfortable enough to spend first-line mobile-fleet assets or scarce trained naval aircrew on a speculative hunt.
future_trigger: Fresh credible RN heavy/carrier track moving east/northeast or repeated interference with Andaman/Bengal bases reopens attack decision; Bay presence alone is not an automatic heavy-surface release.
